idiom_name: public header + single translation unit (opaque handle when instances are needed)
implementation_notes: C has no classes, so the facade is the module boundary itself: a small public header declares the operations, and the .c file includes the subsystem headers, holds the static helpers and keeps any private state. When the subsystem has state or several instances, publish an incomplete type as an opaque handle (typedef struct media_player media_player_t) plus create/destroy functions, so callers can neither see nor allocate the internals. That header/translation-unit split replaces the Facade class; a struct of function pointers (a hand-rolled vtable) is worth the ceremony only when subsystems must be selected at runtime behind one API.
pitfalls: If the public header includes subsystem headers, the boundary is gone: every caller depends on and recompiles against the internals.
A single global facade instance makes more than one configuration impossible and makes tests order-dependent; return a handle instead.
Facade functions that hand out internal pointers or expose the struct body let callers mutate hidden state - keep the type incomplete.
Handles need explicit destroy functions and a documented ownership rule; otherwise the opaque type just hides a leak.
